facts.statement: A Soviet-Chinese expedition uncovered Probactrosaurus remains in Inner Mongolia near Maortu in 1959 and 1960.
facts.quote: In 1959 and 1960 a Soviet-Chinese expedition uncovered the remains of a euornithopod in Inner Mongolia near Maortu.

facts.statement: The type species Probactrosaurus gobiensis was described and named by A. K. Rozhdestvensky in 1966.
facts.quote: The type species is Probactrosaurus gobiensis, described and named by A. K. Rozhdestvensky in 1966.

facts.statement: The specific name gobiensis refers to the Gobi Desert.
facts.quote: The specific name refers to the Gobi Desert.

facts.statement: In 2002, David B. Norman reported that the holotype skull fragment of Probactrosaurus alashanicus was lost after being sent from Moscow to Beijing.
facts.quote: In 2002 David B. Norman published a revision of the genus, in which he reported the holotype specimen of P. alashanicus, the back of a skull, had been lost after being dispatched from Moscow to Beijing.

facts.statement: Lü Junchang named Probactrosaurus mazongshanensis in 1997 based on a holotype found in 1992.
facts.quote: In 1997 Lü Junchang named a third species, Probactrosaurus mazongshanensis, based on holotype IVPP V.11333 found in 1992.

facts.statement: Probactrosaurus mazongshanensis is now considered more closely related to Equijubus and Altirhinus and was moved to the genus Gongpoquansaurus in 2014.
facts.quote: Today, this form is seen as more closely related to Equijubus and Altirhinus rather than to P. gobiensis and is therefore commonly referred to as "Probactrosaurus" mazongshanensis. It was moved to the new genus Gongpoquansaurus in 2014.

facts.statement: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated Probactrosaurus to be 5.5 meters long and weigh one tonne.
facts.quote: Probactrosaurus was a herbivorous dinosaur. In 2010 Gregory S. Paul estimated its length at 5.5 metres (18 feet) and its weight at one tonne.

facts.statement: Probactrosaurus was lightly built with long, slender arms and hands and a small thumb spike.
facts.quote: Probactrosauurus was lightly built, with relatively long and slender arms and hands and only a small thumb spike.

facts.statement: Probactrosaurus was probably predominantly quadrupedal and shared features with later duck-billed dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Probably predominantly quadrupedal, it shared some common features with the later duck-billed dinosaurs.

facts.statement: Probactrosaurus was originally assigned to Iguanodontidae but is now seen as a basal member of Hadrosauroidea closely related to Hadrosauromorpha.
facts.quote: Probactrosaurus was originally assigned by Rozhdestvenky to the Iguanodontidae. Today it is seen as a basal member of the Hadrosauroidea, relatively closely related to the Hadrosauromorpha.

facts.statement: Probactrosaurus lived in Asia during the Early Cretaceous, approximately between 96 and 88 million years ago.
facts.quote: Probactrosaurus gobiensis es la única especie conocida del género extinto Probactrosaurus («antes del Bactrosaurus») de dinosaurio ornitópodo iguanodóntido, que vivió a principios del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre 96 y 88 millones de años, desde el Cenomaniense al Turoniense, en lo que hoy es Asia.

facts.statement: Probactrosaurus lived from the Aptian to the Albian stages, between 121.4 and 100.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Albian (121.4 to 100.5 million years ago)

facts.statement: Probactrosaurus measured between 4 and 6 meters in length and 2.5 meters in height and was a herbivorous dinosaur.
facts.quote: Probactrosaurus midió entre 4 y 6 metros de largo y 2,5 de alto, era un dinosaurio herbívoro.

facts.statement: Probactrosaurus had a large, elongated, and flat head about 1 meter long with a long and narrow snout.
facts.quote: Su cabeza alargada y plana, bastante grande, de 1 metro de longitud, tenía un hocico largo y estrecho.

facts.statement: Probactrosaurus used a toothless beak to strip vegetation and processed it with wide cheek teeth arranged in irregular rows, intermediate between iguanodontids and hadrosauroids.
facts.quote: Tenía un pico sin dientes con el que arrancaba la vegetación y luego la desmenuzaba con los anchos dientes de sus carrillos, que estaban dispuestos en hileras de corte irregular siendo su disposición es intermedia entre los iguanodóntidos y los hadrosáuridos.

facts.statement: Probactrosaurus fossils were found in the Dashuigou Formation in Zizhiqu, Inner Mongolia, China.
facts.quote: Sus fósiles fueron encontrados en la Formación Dashuigou, Zizhiqu, Mongolia Interior, China.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen PIN 2232/1, a partial skeleton with skull, was found in layers of the Dashuigou Formation.
facts.quote: El espécimen holotipo, PIN 2232/1, un esqueleto parcial con cráneo, fue encontrado en capas de la Formación Dashuigou.

facts.statement: Probactrosaurus is considered a representative of Hadrosauroidea within Iguanodontia, though its relationships remain unclear.
facts.quote: Probactrosaurus se considera un representante de Hadrosauroidea dentro de Iguanodontia. Sin embargo, las relaciones no están claras.

facts.statement: A 2010 study by Prieto-Márquez and Norell found that Probactrosaurus is a basal Hadrosauroidea.
facts.quote: Un estudio de Prieto-Márquez y Norell del 2010 encontró que Probactrosaurus es un Hadrosauroidea basal.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the closest relatives of Probactrosaurus are Equijubus and Protohadros.
facts.quote: Los parientes más cercanos son Equijubus y Protohadros.

rejected.statement: Probactrosaurus is an extinct genus of basal hadrosauroid iguanodontian dinosaur that lived in China during the Early Cretaceous period.
rejected.quote: Probactrosaurus (meaning "before Bactrosaurus") is an extinct genus of basal hadrosauroid iguanodontian dinosaur that lived in China during the Early Cretaceous period.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'is an extinct genus of basal hadrosauroid iguanodontian'

rejected.statement: The generic name Probactrosaurus refers to a hypothesis that it was the direct ancestor of Bactrosaurus, a notion now discarded.
rejected.quote: The generic name refers to Rozhdestvensky's hypothesis that Probactrosaurus would be the direct ancestor of Bactrosaurus, a notion now discarded.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'the direct ancestor of Bactrosaurus a notion now'

rejected.statement: The holotype specimen PIN 2232/1, a partial skeleton with skull, was found in the Miaogou Formation near Maortu.
rejected.quote: The holotype specimen, PIN 2232/1, a partial skeleton with skull, was found in layers of the Miaogou Formation (Maortu locality; originally interpreted as the nearby Dashuigou Formation).
